title: Why variation can matter
question: When the food stops, does a reserve chamber change which founders leave living descendants?
intervention: Seeded traits demonstration. Both copies start the same: 24 Sprinters on one sugar meal; every other founder was given a reserve chamber when the dish was made. Copy A keeps stable food: the same meal is added again at 60, 120, 180, 240 and 300 seconds. Copy B gets the first meal only. Run both for 600 seconds and count each founder group's living descendants.
predictedTradeoff: A reserve chamber gives room for 40 more energy but costs 0.02 energy per second as a carried ability plus 0.03 upkeep, and gives no energy by itself. It can only help a Sprinter that has eaten more than it could otherwise hold. Either group may leave more descendants, or neither.
confounds: The reserve chambers were given to alternate founders when the dish was made (present at creation): this is starting variation, not a discovery and not a mutation. Traits are fixed, so no new variation arises during the run. Founders sit at slightly different distances from the centre of the meal. The later meals in copy A are logged as external inputs. Once the copies differ, later encounters differ too: this is one paired run, not proof of a general effect.

all.label: In the single-meal copy, a reserve chamber held energy above the normal cap

completion.journalStamp: Compared founder groups with and without a reserve chamber
